description.narrative: Sveriges kommuner och regioner (SKR) har till Sida ansökt om finansiellt stöd, uppgående till 16,7 milj. sv. kr., för att genomföra ett projekt, benämnt «Support to Decentralisation and Local Self-Government Reform in Armenia», under perioden juli 2022 - december 2023 (etapp 1). Syftet med projektet är att praktiskt kapacitetsstärka det armeniska kommunförbundet, och att genomföra insatser i ett antal pilotkommuner, baserade på en svensk modell för utveckling av lokalt självstyre, och utveckla en långsiktig «roadmap» för utveckling av relationer på demokratisk grund mellan kommunledning och lokalbefolkning, samt utveckling av en kommunal infrastruktur av tillhandahållna tjänster

The Swedish Association of Local Authorities and Regions (SALAR) has applied to Sida for financial support, amounting to SEK 16.7 million. Swed. Cr., to implement a project, entitled «Support to decentralization and Local Self-Government Reform in Armenia», during the period July 2022 - December 2023 (stage 1). The aim of the project is to practically capacity-enhance the Union of Municipalities of Armenia, and to carry out actions in a number of pilot municipalities, based on a Swedish model for the development of local self-government, and develop a long-term «roadmap» for the development of relations on a democratic basis between municipal management and the local population, as well as the development of a municipal infrastructure of services provided

The overall objective of the project is to enhance commitment, capacity, and trust among national and local stakeholders for decentralisation and local self-government reforms in Armenia. It will aim to foster a multi-level policy dialogue as a cross-cutting pathway of change, informed by evidence on institutional conditions and capacities at the local level, and underscored by concrete experiences of improving local self-governance practices.
SALAR focuses its interventions on fiscal decentralisation, decentralisation in the field of education and contributes to objectives linked with wider awareness raising, advocacy and strengthening of strategic reform leadership.
Outcome 1. Institutional framework for decentralisation: actors across levels have aligned in their understanding of the decentralisation and LSG reforms and are prepared for implementation
Outcome 2. Fiscal decentralisation: through collaboration of all actors, fiscal decentralisation is operationalised for the Armenian context. Capacity, tools and processes to implement fiscal decentralisation co-developed by critical actors.
Outcome 3. Sector decentralisation (from 2024 onward): sector ministry (Ministry of Education, Science, Culture and Sports) and LSGs have strengthened capacity and capabilities for management and delivery of delegated decentralised service functions .

title.narrative: Grant Agreement on Support to Decentralisation and Local -Self Government Reform in Armenia
Support to Local Self-Government Reform in Armenia

description.narrative:
Institutional framework for decentralisation: The project has contributed to better alignment in the understanding of decentralisation with project partners. After the launch of DeaLoG in 2023, a first breaking point in the perception and awareness of the decentralisation reforms by selected government officials was reached through two study visits to Sweden. SALAR have built up partnerships and mutual trust with national stakeholders during a study visit to Sweden and through ongoing contacts and meetings with key partner ministries (Ministry of Territorial Administration, Ministry of Finance and Ministry of Education, Science, Culture and Sports), as well as the Deputy Prime-Minister Office and the Standing Committee on Territorial Administration, Local Self-Governance, Agriculture and Environment Protection of the National Assembly. The study visits also laid out ways on how to integrate SALAR methodologies and expertise to improve national and local government decision-making in the education and fiscal sectors. The project has started an initiative to develop a common language and unified forms of communication on decentralisation reforms in Armenia to be used both for the donor community and for key stakeholders at national and local level.
Fiscal decentralisation: The project has contributed to more awareness of the importance of reforming fiscal policy with its project partners. There is understanding of the necessity of implementing pilot activities to build trust between central and local government authorities, even if capacity still needs to be strengthened in key areas of the Ministry of Finance. The Project now has an internal resource in Ministry of Finance to work with staff on methodologies of relevance to fiscal decentralisation, which has a significant impact on overall understanding of the preparations for fiscal decentralisation. Within its efforts to promote the participatory budgeting at local level, the MoF decided to enhance the capacities of the municipalities through extended and more active dialogue and engagement with both municipalities and local CSOs, presenting in details the new subversion scheme (which has been elaborated with technical support from DeaLoG project) for the financing the projects of municipalities developed through participation mechanism.
Sector decentralisation (from 2024 onward): Initially, the outcome 3 was not part of the result matrix as such. In the beginning of the project, there was no clarity for sector priorities and Outcome 3 as a growth area. It was planned to use the period from March 2023-March 2024 as a preparatory phase for selection of the sector and planning the respective activities. The final decision on the education sector was made in summer 2023, followed by a joint action plan with Ministry of Education. Preparation for the planned decentralisation steps in the area of education decentralisation is front and centre for SALARs approach in Armenia. As part of discussions on a sectoral component of decentralisation, SALAR agreed with Ministry of Education Science, Culture and Sports on a workplan and began an initiative focused on stimulating school-municipal cooperation and community development. This will provide evidence for national decision makers concerning the decentralisation of the education sector in the project cost-extension period. During the implementation period, the project achieved a result with a more pronounced strategic focus on the education sector being developed. A progress was made to empower municipalities around school management, one of the few areas that is now actively being decentralised by the government.
